---
title: "Infer and compare gene regulatory networks"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(error = FALSE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
	eval = isTRUE(getOption("scop.grn.tutorials", FALSE)))
```

## Run the pancreas example

This tutorial uses the 1,000 mouse pancreas cells packaged with scop. It fits
direct TF-gene links, reads the native result, draws a network, and scores its
predicted target programs with existing scop functions.

Run the code chunks interactively after loading scop. To execute the main
example while rendering this article, set `options(scop.grn.tutorials = TRUE)`.
The separate environment and external-data recipes below run after their inputs
have been prepared.

```{r pancreas-input}
library(scop)
data("pancreas_sub", package = "scop")
pancreas <- Seurat::NormalizeData(pancreas_sub, assay = "RNA", verbose = FALSE)
expression <- SeuratObject::LayerData(pancreas, assay = "RNA", layer = "data")
variance <- Matrix::rowMeans(expression^2) - Matrix::rowMeans(expression)^2
targets <- names(sort(variance, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(64L)]
regulators <- intersect(
	c("Pdx1", "Nkx6-1", "Neurod1", "Pax6", "Isl1", "Arx", "Rfx6"),
	rownames(expression)
)
stopifnot(length(regulators) > 0L, all(is.finite(variance[targets])))
```

The target rule and TF list are fixed before fitting. This small candidate set
keeps the example quick to run. Use the candidate set appropriate for your own
analysis when fitting a full network. The example retains the two highest
importance regulator edges per target.

```{r pancreas-network}
work_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "scop-pancreas-grn")
pancreas <- RunGRN(
	pancreas, assay = "RNA", layer = "data",
	methods = "GRNBoost2", backend = "cpp",
	regulators = regulators, targets = targets,
	method_args = list(n_rounds = 100L, max_edges_per_target = 2L),
	work_dir = work_dir,
	cores = 1L, seed = 1201L, verbose = FALSE
)
head(GetGRN(pancreas))
result <- GetGRN(pancreas, what = "result")
result$implementation
result$package_versions
```

`methods` chooses the method. `backend` chooses an available implementation.
The result records the actual `implementation`, package versions, effective
parameters, and execution details. For example, the scop C++ GRNBoost2 route and
the official Arboreto route have separate implementation identities.

A Seurat input returns the updated object with its complete network in
`tools`. A matrix input returns the `TF`, `target`, `importance` edge table by
default. Set `return_type = "result"` to obtain the complete result directly,
or `return_type = "edges"` to obtain the edge table from a Seurat input.

```{r pancreas-inspect}
edges <- GetGRN(pancreas, what = "edges", layer = "tf_gene")
native <- GetGRN(pancreas, what = "native")
parameters <- GetGRN(pancreas, what = "parameters")
stopifnot(identical(edges$raw_score, native$importance))
head(edges[, c("source", "target", "raw_score", "score_type", "sign", "sign_basis")])
parameters
```

GRNBoost2 importance is a nonnegative feature-importance score. Its sign is
unknown in the standard view. Signed methods retain their own coefficient or
correlation evidence. Each edge also records its direction and entity types.

```{r pancreas-network-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
GRNPlot(pancreas, type = "network", top_n = 50L,
	title = "Pancreas TF-gene candidates")
```

`top_n` limits the displayed view. `GetGRN(pancreas, what = "native")` continues to
return the complete native result.

## Score the predicted target programs

`GetGRN(..., what = "gene_sets")` returns native gene sets when the method
provides them. Otherwise, it groups direct TF-gene targets by source and sign.
The `unknown` suffix preserves an unknown sign. These gene sets describe
predicted target programs.

```{r pancreas-score}
programs <- GetGRN(pancreas, what = "gene_sets")
programs <- programs[lengths(programs) >= 5L]
stopifnot(length(programs) > 0L)
pancreas <- CellScoring(
	pancreas, features = programs, assay = "RNA", layer = "data",
	method = "UCell", backend = "cpp", name = "GRN",
	minGSSize = 5L, classification = FALSE, store_metadata = TRUE,
	cores = 1L, verbose = FALSE
)
score_columns <- make.names(paste("GRN", names(programs), sep = "_"))
score_columns <- intersect(score_columns, colnames(pancreas[[]]))
stopifnot(length(score_columns) > 0L)
```

The packaged input contains counts and cell labels. Compute an embedding before
using `FeatureDimPlot`.

```{r pancreas-embedding}
embedding_genes <- union(targets, regulators)
pancreas <- Seurat::ScaleData(pancreas, assay = "RNA", features = embedding_genes,
	verbose = FALSE)
pancreas <- Seurat::RunPCA(pancreas, assay = "RNA", features = embedding_genes,
	npcs = 10L, verbose = FALSE)
pancreas <- Seurat::RunUMAP(pancreas, reduction = "pca", dims = 1:10,
	seed.use = 1201L, verbose = FALSE)
```

```{r pancreas-program-map, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
FeatureDimPlot(pancreas, features = head(score_columns, 2L), reduction = "umap")
```

```{r pancreas-program-heatmap, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
GroupHeatmap(pancreas, features = score_columns, group.by = "CellType",
	layer = "data", exp_method = "raw")
```

## Switch the inference method

Use the same candidates with a different method name. This PPCOR recipe needs
the optional `ppcor` R package. PPCOR reports partial correlations with
`directed = FALSE`; its source and target columns define a table view of an
association network.

```{r pancreas-ppcor, eval=FALSE}
PrepareEnv(modules = "ppcor", components = "r")
ppcor_grn <- RunGRN(
	pancreas, assay = "RNA", layer = "data", methods = "PPCOR",
	regulators = regulators, targets = targets,
	method_args = list(method = "spearman"), return_type = "result",
	work_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "scop-pancreas-ppcor"), verbose = FALSE
)
head(GetGRN(ppcor_grn))
GRNPlot(ppcor_grn, top_n = 50L)
GRNPlot(pancreas, type = "overlap", compare = list(PPCOR = ppcor_grn), top_n = 50L)
```

Overlap views compare edge identities within the common typed entity space.
Each method keeps its own scores and ranking. The view also retains edge
direction, so an undirected association differs from a directed TF-gene link.

For the official Arboreto GRNBoost2 implementation, prepare its Python profile
once and select that implementation explicitly. You can also point to an
existing interpreter without changing the Python interpreter of your R session.

```{r official-python, eval=FALSE}
PrepareEnv(modules = "grnboost2", configure_runtime = FALSE)
official_grn <- RunGRN(
	pancreas, assay = "RNA", layer = "data", methods = "grnboost2",
	backend = "python", regulators = regulators, targets = targets,
	return_type = "result",
	work_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "scop-pancreas-arboreto"),
	cores = 1L, seed = 1201L
)
```

Method-specific parameters belong in `method_args`. Unknown names and repeated
top-level arguments are reported before inference. Put interpreter selection in
the reserved `method_args$runtime` list, for example
`list(python = "/path/to/environment/bin/python", timeout = 3600)`.

## Fit groups separately

`group.by` defines separate network fits. It is independent of downstream
program-score summaries. Select `groups` explicitly and use a complete result
for more than one group.

```{r pancreas-grouped, eval=FALSE}
grouped <- RunGRN(
	pancreas, assay = "RNA", layer = "data", methods = "grnboost2",
	regulators = regulators, targets = targets,
	group.by = "CellType", groups = c("Ductal", "Endocrine"),
	method_args = list(n_rounds = 100L), return_type = "result",
	work_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "scop-pancreas-groups"), verbose = FALSE
)
GetGRN(grouped, group = "Endocrine")
GetGRN(grouped, all_groups = TRUE)
```

## Supply time by cell ID

LEAP, SCODE, and SINCERITIES require measured time or a supplied pseudotime.
This example reads a BEELINE `VSC-2000-3-50` case. The expression CSV has genes
in rows and cell IDs in columns. The time CSV has cell IDs in rows and named
trajectories in columns. Set `beeline_dir` to your downloaded case directory.

The example selects 120 cells on the first trajectory and eight genes by a
fixed variance rule. It uses the supplied times throughout.

```{r beeline-time-input, eval=FALSE}
beeline_dir <- "/path/to/VSC-2000-3-50"
time_expression <- as.matrix(utils::read.csv(
	file.path(beeline_dir, "ExpressionData.csv"), row.names = 1L, check.names = FALSE
))
time_table <- as.matrix(utils::read.csv(
	file.path(beeline_dir, "PseudoTime.csv"), row.names = 1L, check.names = FALSE
))
time_cells <- rownames(time_table)[is.finite(time_table[, 1L])]
time_cells <- head(time_cells, 120L)
time_expression <- time_expression[, time_cells, drop = FALSE]
time_variance <- apply(time_expression, 1L, stats::var)
time_genes <- names(sort(time_variance, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(8L)]
time_expression <- time_expression[time_genes, , drop = FALSE]
pseudotime <- stats::setNames(time_table[time_cells, 1L], time_cells)
time_regulators <- time_genes[1:3]
time_targets <- time_genes[4:8]
```

```{r beeline-time-network, eval=FALSE}
PrepareEnv(modules = c("leap", "scode", "sincerities"), components = "r")
time_fits <- list()
time_settings <- list(
	leap = list(max_lag_prop = 1/3),
	scode = list(latent_dim = 3L, n_iter = 25L, n_runs = 2L),
	sincerities = list(max_time_points = 6L, SIGN = 1L)
)
for (method in names(time_settings)) {
	time_fits[[method]] <- RunGRN(
		time_expression, methods = method, pseudotime = pseudotime,
		regulators = time_regulators, targets = time_targets,
		method_args = time_settings[[method]], return_type = "result",
		work_dir = file.path(tempdir(), paste0("scop-beeline-", method)),
		cores = 1L, seed = 1201L, verbose = FALSE
	)
}
GRNPlot(time_fits$leap, top_n = 15L)
```

Pseudotime vectors must have cell-ID names. A trajectory matrix may contain
branch-specific missing values for LEAP. Choose one complete trajectory with
`method_args$trajectory` for SCODE or SINCERITIES when supplying several columns.

## Keep a reusable result

```{r save-network}
result_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "pancreas-grn.rds")
saveRDS(pancreas, result_file)
reloaded <- readRDS(result_file)
stopifnot(identical(GetGRN(pancreas), GetGRN(reloaded)))
```

A single stored network is selected automatically. If the object contains
several networks, use `tool_name` in `GetGRN()` or `GRNPlot()`. The default
storage name is `GRN_<method>`; set `tool_name` when fitting to keep more than
one run of the same method. Replacing an existing entry requires
`overwrite = TRUE`.

Completed cache records include input, candidate, time, parameter, runtime, and
resource identities. Reusing the same request verifies its completed result.
Changing a scientific input creates a different request. `force = TRUE`
requests another computation while retaining execution evidence.

## Choose a network method

The 14 methods below are the manuscript comparison methods. RegDiffusion and
SCENIC remain available as additional scop methods.

| Method name | Input | Evidence retained by the complete result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `multicsn` | RNA, or paired RNA and ATAC | Independent endpoint coefficients, deletion evidence, ordinal weights, and supported chains |
| `genie3` | RNA | Tree-based TF-gene importance |
| `grnboost2` | RNA | Boosting importance with explicit C++ or official Arboreto identity |
| `gniplr` | RNA | Native polynomial-regression scores and implementation identity |
| `ppcor` | RNA | Undirected partial correlation and its statistics |
| `pidc` | RNA | Undirected information-theoretic association |
| `scorpion` | RNA, with optional priors | Native network scores and supplied prior configuration |
| `scsgl` | RNA | Undirected signed graph scores |
| `leap` | RNA and time | Lagged correlations after cell-ID alignment |
| `scode` | RNA and time | Native dynamical coefficients and repeated-fit aggregation |
| `sincerities` | RNA and time | Native distribution-regression scores and explicit `SIGN` setting |
| `pando` | Paired RNA and ATAC | Native interaction coefficients, modules, and membership projections |
| `linger` | Paired counts and bulk reference | Native TF-gene, TF-region, and region-gene scores |
| `scenicplus` or `SCENIC+` | Prepared paired multiome inputs and motif resources | Official SCENIC+ layers, direct and extended eRegulons, and AUC |

See [the paired multiome tutorial](grn-multiome.html) for multiCSN, Pando,
LINGER, and official SCENIC+. Runtime and package versions are retained in each
computed result, so execution evidence stays attached to the selected method.
